sections.html:
The Greene County Recorder is on the third floor of 69 Greene St. in Xenia. The recorder's page gives two sets of weekday hours: the counter is staffed until 4:00 p.m., but recording stops at 3:00 p.m. A deed that arrives after that sits until the next business day, so on closing day plan to get documents there early.

The office keeps the permanent land records for the whole county. A seller will run into several of these filings during a sale:

  • Deeds, mortgages and releases of mortgage
  • Easements, leases and land contracts
  • Affidavits, trusts and powers of attorney
  • Mechanic's liens, federal tax liens and child support liens
  • Plats, condominium documents and annexations

The office also files and certifies military discharges. Those records are closed to the public, and the person discharged or their heirs can get a copy free of charge.

sections.h2: Steps before a Greene County deed is recorded
sections.html:
Start at the auditor's office, not the recorder. The transfer desk there wants a completed Statement of Value (DTE 100) or the exempt version (DTE 100 EX), fees payable to the auditor, the grantor's name spelled exactly as it appears on the grantor's own deed, and map department initials. The grantor signs, and a notary acknowledges the signature.

R.C. 5301.01 lists who may take that acknowledgment, from notaries and mayors to court clerks, auditors and engineers. Recording protects the buyer too. Under R.C. 5301.25, a deed that is never recorded is treated as fraudulent against a later purchaser who bought in good faith without notice of it.

If the land is in the CAUV farm program, in the filing year or the year before, attach that program's conveyance statement. If a survey was done, the deed has to carry the surveyor's name.

sections.h2: What recording a deed costs in Greene County
sections.html:
R.C. 317.32 sets the fee schedule, and each charge pairs a base amount with an equal housing trust fund amount. Senate Bill 94 allows as much as $5.00 more per document, but a January 2, 2026 notice from the Greene County Recorder says standard fees stay the same.

Recording fees under R.C. 317.32
ServiceBase feeHousing trust fund fee
Record and index, first two pages$17$17
Each added page$4$4
Marginal reference by separate instrument$2$2
Certified copy, per page$1$1
Document preservation surchargeUp to $5None

Copies cost less if you make them yourself: $.10 a page for self-service official copies, against $2.00 a page when staff make them.

The auditor collects these before the deed goes to the recorder. The county's transfer page shows a combined $2.00 per thousand dollars of purchase price, made up of a $1.00 conveyance fee and a $1.00 transfer fee, plus $0.50 per parcel. An online calculator is posted on the same page.

The grantor owes the tax. R.C. 322.02 caps a county's own transfer tax at 30 cents per hundred dollars of value. Some transfers carry no fee under R.C. 319.54, including these:

  • Moves among heirs or devisees of one decedent where no money is paid
  • Gifts between spouses or from parent to child
  • Deeds into a revocable trust, and back out to the grantor
  • Deeds given only to secure or release a debt

The reason for the exemption is written on the statement, so go over it with the closing agent before anyone signs.

sections.h2: Liens that can turn up against a Greene County seller
sections.html:
The recorder files several kinds of liens, and a buyer's title company searches for each one under the seller's name and the parcel. The county's list covers mechanic's liens, Medicaid fraud liens, federal tax liens, child support liens, unemployment compensation liens, personal tax liens and workers' compensation liens. A Notice of Commencement is filed here as well.

Fees differ by lien type under the Ohio Recorders' Association fee table:

  • Federal tax lien (IRS): $5.00, with $3.00 to release it.
  • Unemployment compensation lien and workers' compensation lien: no fee.
  • Personal property tax lien and Medicaid fraud lien: no fee.
  • Mechanic's lien and its release: the standard per-page fee.

If you know about a lien, ask the lienholder for a recorded release well before closing day. Once the release is filed it shows up in the same index as the original lien, and the title examiner can clear the exception.

sections.h2: Deed forms used in Greene County sales
sections.html:
The state fee table names the usual choices, all recorded at the same per-page rates: warranty, limited warranty, quit claim and survivorship deeds. Estate and trust sales bring executor's, administrator's, guardian's or trustee's deeds, depending on who holds authority. A transfer on death designation affidavit is also recorded here.

Survivorship deeds fall under R.C. 5302.20. Language showing clear intent creates the tenancy, and a conveyance signed by every tenant ends it. Co-owners who inherited together should read the recorded deed to see whether they hold in survivorship or in common, since that decides who has to sign the sale deed.

sections.h2: Where Greene County land is recorded
sections.html:
Land is recorded in the county where it sits, so parcels in every city, village and township here go through the Xenia office. Beavercreek, Bellbrook, Fairborn and Xenia are the cities, and Kettering reaches into Greene County even though most of it is in Montgomery County.

The auditor's rolls hold more than 73,000 parcels. Each has its own chain of recorded documents, and a buyer's title search reads that chain back through earlier deeds. A gap in it can slow a sale, so a seller who has an old unrecorded deed or a missing release in the file should fix it before listing.

sections.h2: Searching records and finding a mortgage release
sections.html:
Online, the Recorder's Document Search covers filings from 1984 onward. Images on the website carry a watermark, and a watermarked page cannot be submitted for recording, so get clean copies at the counter. A transfer tracking table shows where a newly submitted transfer stands, and a fraud alert service can notify an owner when something is filed against a registered property.

A lender gets 90 days after payoff to file the release or satisfaction of mortgage. An owner who paid off a loan long ago should look up that release before listing, since a missing one can stall a closing. If it never was filed, contact the lender and ask for one to be recorded.

Greene County had 68,166 households in the 2020 to 2024 survey, averaging 2.38 people, and roughly 74,000 housing units in 2025. Monthly owner costs have a median of $1,702 with a mortgage and $700 without one. Builders pulled 567 permits in 2025.

sections.h2: What to bring to the Greene County office
sections.html:
For a standard sale the closing agent usually handles the paperwork, but it helps to know the order. First the auditor reviews the Statement of Value and collects the transfer charges. Then the signed, notarized deed goes to the recorder, who records and indexes it. After recording, the buyer gets the original back.

A seller handling things directly should bring the signed deed, the completed DTE form, any survey or farm program statement, and payment for the auditor's fees. Bring a separate payment for the recorder's fees. Arrive before 3:00 p.m. so the deed is recorded the same day.

faqs.q: When does Greene County stop recording documents each day?
faqs.a: At 3:00 p.m. on weekdays, with recording starting at 7:30 a.m. The office itself stays open until 4:00 p.m., so bring anything urgent early in the day.

faqs.q: Did Greene County raise recording fees after the state change?
faqs.a: Not for standard documents. A January 2, 2026 recorder notice says fees stay put, although Senate Bill 94 permits up to $5.00 more.

faqs.q: Which office collects the Greene County transfer charge?
faqs.a: The auditor collects it from the grantor before recording. The county shows $2.00 per thousand dollars of price and a $0.50 per-parcel charge.

faqs.q: How do I get a copy of my Greene County deed?
faqs.a: Go to 69 Greene St., third floor, or use the online document search. Self-service official copies cost $.10 a page, and staff-made ones cost $2.00 a page.

faqs.q: How soon must a lender record a mortgage release in Greene County?
faqs.a: Within ninety days of payoff. The recorder holds the release, and copies come from the counter or the document search.
